clue.text: Port deprived of five hundred and six deliveries?

indicators.note: a port deprived of something has had that thing taken away from its name

parts.note: Dover is the English Channel port
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: A harbour town loses its 506 shipments, a cargo puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' sounds like freight, but in cricket a bowler delivers balls, and six of them make a set.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a bowler's set of six balls, each called a delivery, is an over.

clue.text: The old man going to the forefront leading English dance

indicators.note: these pieces come in front of the next one, leading it in the word

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, one's old man
the van, short for vanguard, is the forefront

explanation.surface: Dad pushes to the front of an English dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A pavane is a stately court dance of the sixteenth century.

clue.text: Bosses once associated with City of London

definitions.note: exec, short for executive, is used collectively for the management, the bosses

parts.note: ex means former, once
EC is the postcode district of the City of London

explanation.surface: Former bosses who once had links to London's financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: EC (East Central) is the postal area covering the City, London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Executives are senior managers, and exec is the short informal form.

clue.text: Architect to splash out endlessly on church

indicators.note: said of a word, endlessly means its final letter is cut off

parts.note: to splash out is to spend lavishly
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An architect spends without limit on a church building project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the last letter off SPEND, leaving SPEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Basil Spence was the architect of the rebuilt Coventry Cathedral.

clue.text: They have schemes they map out on paper

definitions.meaning: people or devices that plot points or routes on a chart

explanation.surface: Schemers who draw up their plans on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To plot is both to conspire and to mark positions on a chart, so plotters do both.

clue.text: Study AV for example to see what happened to Saul

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
the AV, the Authorised Version, is a version of the Bible

explanation.surface: Read the King James Bible to learn about Saul's story.
explanation.walkthrough: AV is the Authorised (King James) Version of the Bible; Saul became the apostle Paul on the road to Damascus.
explanation.definitionFit: Saul of Tarsus underwent a famous religious change of faith on the Damascus road.

clue.text: A Roman road beguiles, they say? I'll take a higher route!

parts.note: via is the Latin for road

indicators.note: they say signals that the word before is only heard, not spelt

parts.note: to beguile is to trick, so beguiles is tricks

explanation.surface: Someone tempted off an old Roman road decides to rise above it.
explanation.walkthrough: TRICKS sounds like TRIX, and 'they say' marks that.
explanation.definitionFit: A female pilot flies, taking a route far above any road.

clue.text: It could mean gathering great 'oard into circle

indicators.note: into means the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: a ring is a circle
a great hoard is a heap; the apostrophe drops its h as a Cockney would, leaving 'eap

explanation.surface: A Cockney's big stash is gathered into a circle.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'oard shows the dropped H, so HEAP loses its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaping is cutting and gathering in a crop at harvest.

clue.text: Support one kind of prisoner — it's bad being kept in

indicators.note: being kept in means held inside the other piece

parts.note: a POW is a prisoner of war
ill means bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: A captured soldier is badly treated while locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillow is a cushion that supports the head in bed.

clue.text: Give resources to a US lawyer — one needs to keep afloat

parts.note: to arm is to equip or supply with weapons
a DA is an American District Attorney

explanation.surface: Funding an American attorney who needs help staying financially afloat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep afloat' sounds like staying solvent, but it means literally floating: a fleet of ships.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a fleet of warships, which must stay on the water.

clue.text: Fellow resident concerned with psychological processes

parts.note: co- means fellow, as in co-worker
a native is someone born and living in a place, a resident

explanation.surface: A neighbour who lives nearby takes an interest in psychology.
explanation.definitionFit: Conative is a psychology term for conation, the mental faculty of willing and striving.

clue.text: Rebuke insane oaf with a leer that's nasty

indicators.note: nasty treatment of these letters here means they are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Tell off a crazed lout who leers nastily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's nasty' signals rearranging INSANE OAF and A LEER together.
explanation.definitionFit: To send someone away with a flea in their ear is to give them a sharp telling-off.

clue.text: A fir, we may deduce, in recreational area

parts.note: read the answer as wordplay

explanation.surface: Spotting a fir tree, one infers there is a park nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer, read as an instruction, means 'grind up FAIR', and that produces the clue's A FIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground is an open space where fairs, rides and amusements are set up.

clue.text: Tree healthier-looking after being pollarded?

indicators.note: a pollarded tree has its top cut off, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: rosier means pinker in the cheeks, healthier-looking

explanation.surface: A tree looks in better health once it has been cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: Pollarding lops the top, so ROSIER loses its first letter R; in a down entry the first letter is literally the top.
explanation.definitionFit: An osier is a kind of willow, grown for its supple branches used in basketry.

clue.text: Dig rock, needing energy

parts.note: the Rock is Gibraltar, called Gib for short
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Excavate some rock, which takes plenty of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dig' looks like excavating, but it is a jibe or taunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A dig is a sly cutting remark, which is what a gibe is.

clue.text: Travel into troubled cities, thinking little of others

indicators.note: into places the first piece inside the second
troubled means disturbed, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A selfish traveller heads into cities in turmoil without a thought for others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges the city letters to EISTIC; 'into' then sets the travel word inside, so the surface's journey is the mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: An egoistic person is self-centred, putting their own interests first.

clue.text: In report gloss over mutual-aid organisation

indicators.note: a report is something spoken, so the word before is to be heard, not read

parts.note: to gild is to cover with a thin golden layer, glossing over flaws

explanation.surface: A report whitewashes the failings of a cooperative society.
explanation.definitionFit: A guild is an association of craftsmen or traders formed for mutual help and protection.

clue.text: Shortage of wind — oxygen needed for asthmatic initially

indicators.note: needed for here means one letter takes the place of another

parts.note: a draught is a current of air, a wind

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word after

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A short-winded asthmatic first needs an oxygen supply.
explanation.walkthrough: In DRAUGHT the A (from 'asthmatic initially') is swapped for O.
explanation.definitionFit: A drought is a long lack of rain, a severe shortage of water.

clue.text: Do without someone to lead the team

definitions.meaning: to go without it, as in skipping a meal
the captain of a curling or bowls team, short for skipper

explanation.surface: Manage without a captain for the side.
explanation.definitionFit: Skipping means missing out on something, and the skip captains a curling or bowls rink.

clue.text: Useless as person volunteering for charity work?

definitions.meaning: read literally, a volunteer does ..., working unpaid

explanation.surface: Dismissing a charity volunteer as worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer: doing good for nothing means working for no pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A good-for-nothing is an idle, worthless person, and a volunteer does good without pay.

clue.text: One going into a number as a loud performer

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
an actor is a performer

explanation.surface: A noisy performer joins a musical number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' suggests a song, but it is mathematical: a factor divides into it.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic a factor is a number that divides exactly into another.

clue.text: Group knowing a bit

parts.note: hep, an old form of hip, means in the know
a tad is a little bit

explanation.surface: A group of people who know a little about something.
explanation.definitionFit: A heptad is a set or group of seven.

clue.text: Greek island dispenses with old Russian people

parts.note: Cos (Kos) is an island in the Dodecanese
to sack is to dismiss, to dispense with someone

explanation.surface: A Greek island lays off its old Russian workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Cossacks were a people of southern Russia and Ukraine famed as horsemen.

clue.text: What sounds like steep part of old England

indicators.note: these words say the answer is heard as the next word

parts.note: to steep is to soak

explanation.surface: A sloping district in medieval England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steep' looks like an adjective about a slope, but it is the verb, to soak.
explanation.definitionFit: A soke was an old English jurisdiction, a district under a lord's court.

clue.text: See in cup knocked over a soft mineral

indicators.note: a cup knocked over is upside down, so the letters read backwards
in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a mug is a cup
to spy is to see

explanation.surface: Look at a cup tipped over, spilling chalky powder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' makes MUSPYG, and 'knocked over' turns that whole thing round, as a tipped cup would be.
explanation.definitionFit: Gypsum is a soft calcium sulphate mineral used to make plaster.

clue.text: Language heard from Cockney Liverpudlian Bob?

indicators.note: the next word is to be spoken in an accent that drops its h and, as in Liverpool, says hair like her

parts.note: a bob is a short haircut, a hairdo

explanation.surface: A language spoken by a Liverpool man called Bob with a London accent.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys drop the H and Scousers (Liverpudlians) say 'hair' like 'her', so HAIRDO comes out as 'urdu.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is the national language of Pakistan, also widely spoken in India.

clue.text: At home, woman needs match for particular colour

parts.note: in means at home
Di is a woman's name, short for Diana
to go is to match, as colours that go together

explanation.surface: A woman at home wants something that goes with her colour scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep blue-violet, one of the colours of the rainbow.

clue.text: Asian capital with Sikh symbol and spiritual essence of the French

parts.note: K stands for the five Ks, the articles of faith whose names start with K
in Hinduism the atman is the soul, one's spiritual essence
du is French for of the

explanation.surface: A capital city blending Sikh symbolism with French spirituality.
explanation.definitionFit: Katmandu, usually spelt Kathmandu, is the capital city of Nepal.
